title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Arielle Chen
description:
Motivation: the paged KV cache was allocating and freeing page blocks aggressively during mixed-length workloads which increases GC pressure and causes tail latency spikes for long-running chat sessions. This PR implements two complementary optimizations: 1) a block allocator that reuses freed blocks from a small fast-path free list to avoid repeated allocations under churn, and 2) locality-aware pinning heuristics so blocks that are repeatedly accessed by the same request/worker are preferentially pinned to avoid eviction while still allowing global reuse. The changes are behind a feature flag (kv.paged_allocator_reuse=true) and include a conservative default pin TTL. This is an internal runtime optimization (no API changes).

What I changed: consolidated allocator code into paged_kv/block_allocator.{h,cc}, added a lock-free per-worker free-list fast-path with a fallback global free pool; added metrics for allocator hits/misses and pinned_evictions; introduced a locality score to block metadata and a pin manager that uses per-request affinity to decide pin duration; added unit and stress tests covering concurrency and eviction edge cases; added canary job config in perf-canary for new benchmark runs.

Checklist:
- [x] allocator reuse fast-path + global pool
- [x] locality-aware pinning with TTL and dynamic decay
- [x] metrics and tracing hooks (allocator.hits, allocator.reuse_rate, kv.pins, kv.pin_evictions)
- [x] unit + stress tests
- [x] perf canary results attached
- [x] feature flag + safe defaults

Testing & results: ran perf-canary workload (mixed-length chat + streaming sampling) across a 4-GPU serving pool. Observed ~7-12% P50 latency reduction and 15-22% throughput improvement on heavy sampling scenarios where KV churn was high. Tail (P99) latency improved ~9% in long-conversation traces due to reduced eviction-induced recompute. Canary logs and metrics exported to the perf dashboard (link in Linear ticket ENG-912).

Rollout plan: enable flag in dedicated clusters first (low risk), monitor allocator.metrics and kv.pin_evictions. If stable after 2 weeks, flip default in hosted environments. Backout: revert flag or set kv.paged_allocator_reuse=false; code stays behind the flag so safe to toggle.

Notes: follow-up work (ENG-934) will explore adaptive TTL based on request types and extending locality scoring across sharded workers.
